text:
alex: Heads-up — I'm seeing tail latency blips in the quota layer during short client spikes (100-300 req/s bursts for ~10-30s). Not sure if it's our refill jitter or the way we surface metrics.
priya: Can you paste a sample timeline? which metric shows the blip?
alex: Uploading a small snippet: `pct_99_latency_ms` jumps from 40 -> 230 for spike windows. Token_consumption per-key shows a sharp dip then catch-up.
ben: That sounds like aggressive smoothing + aggressive drain on refill. Are we using hierarchical buckets (org -> key) or single token stream?
alex: Hierarchical: org pool then per-key sub-bucket. But per-key refills are edge-cased when org pool has been drawn down. Seems fine for long steady traffic but creates dropouts on short spikes.
sasha-bot: deploy: quota-service v2.8.1 deployed to canary at 1913503010.
priya: Hypothesis: small spikes exhaust per-key instant credit and the org-level refill only wakes up on its 1s tick; the per-key smoothing averages hide the micro-recovery. We should try smaller refill granularity or local fast-path borrow.
lina: UX note — operators need a cheap way to see "short-spike forgiveness" on the console, like a toggle and a chart of 5s vs 1min rates. Current dashboard is 1m granularity and looks like a meltdown.
theo: Agreed. For telemetry we can emit a sampled event for any request that encountered a transient 429 or exceeded burst credits. Include: key, org, seq_len, bucket_level_before, bucket_level_after, and boolean "borrowed_from_org". Sample rate 1/1000 by default.
ben: Sounds good but sampling 1/1000 might miss short noisy clients. Suggest 1/100 for keys that exceed a threshold of short spikes/day, and 1/1000 otherwise. We can keep this dynamic.
alex: Could also record a counter metric: spike_recoveries_{key,org} with tags short_window=5s and long_window=60s. That helps show if short spikes get smoothed out.
priya: On enforcement algorithm: two quick options — (A) reduce per-key refill interval to 100ms with jitter, keep token rate same; (B) implement a tiny transient credit reserve that can be consumed for <=30s and then refilled from org budget gradually. Thoughts?
lina: Option B would be easier to explain in the UI: "burst buffer (30s)" toggle. Option A is more transparent but might increase token churn noise in metrics.
theo: Option B needs careful accounting to avoid org-level starvation. Proposal: reserve at most 5% of org pool per key as ephemeral buffer, and only if org_pool>threshold. Emit telemetry when reserve used.
ben: Quick sim I ran: with ephemeral 5% buffer size and a drain-recovery half-life of 15s, 99th latency drops ~45% for 10-30s spikes in our test traces. No measurable steady-state cost.
alex: Nice. Implementation plan? Small change in quota-service plus a console flag. We should also add a rollout with canary + 2% then 20% then 100% if no regression.
sasha-bot: alert: canary failed at 1913503600 — one instance returned 429 spikes after 27s. Deploy rolled back automatically.
priya: Can handle — sounds like we need telemetry hooks to capture root cause. Alex, can you paste the token log around that 27s?
alex: Here — snippet: ```
[1913503593] key=client-42 org=org-a bucket_key=perkey level_before=12 level_after=0 borrowed=false
[1913503594] key=client-42 org=org-a request=1 tokens=60 allowed=false  # short burst > per-key cap
[1913503594] org_pool_level=120 borrowed_attempt=true borrow_allowed=false
[1913503595] bucket_replenish_tick: perkey +6 org -6
```
lina: That matches: borrow_attempt failed because org_pool already below borrow threshold. With ephemeral buffer option, that request would have succeeded and only consumed the buffer. Perfect use-case.
theo: Action items: 1) ben to turn on ephemeral buffer sim across traces and send metrics (ETA 2d). 2) alex to sketch quota-service changes + contract for telemetry events (ETA EOD). 3) lina to add a console mock for burst buffer toggle + 5s/60s chart (ETA 3d). 4) priya to draft rollout plan with sampled telemetry gating (ETA 1d).
ben: I'll also run a quick sensitivity test on reserve size (1%, 3%, 5%, 10%) and post results.
alex: I'll include an example config snippet for the API and the ops flag: ```
quota.ephemeral_buffer.enabled=true
quota.ephemeral_buffer.size_percent=5
quota.ephemeral_buffer.max_duration_s=30
quota.refill.per_key_interval_ms=100  # only if ephemeral disabled
quota.telemetry.spike_sample_rate_default=0.01
quota.telemetry.spike_sample_rate_high=0.1
```
priya: LGTM. One more ask — we should add a per-route override for latency-sensitive endpoints so they get a slightly larger ephemeral buffer.
lina: Good call. I'll wire a UI control to attach route-level policies.
sasha-bot: reminder: incident runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quota-burst.md
alex: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short RFC tomorrow and attach the sim graphs. :thumbsup:
priya: :thumbsup:
ben: :rocket:
